blogs.title: Young, autoantibody‑negative, and not quite type 2: a pragmatic MODY workup at the bedside
blogs.description: This post lays out a stepwise approach to distinguishing MODY from type 1 and type 2 diabetes in a young adult. We highlight high-yield clues from the case: multi‑generational early‑onset diabetes, marked postprandial hyperglycemia on OGTT, glycosuria from a low renal glucose threshold, negative GAD/IA‑2/ZnT8, and preserved stimulated C‑peptide (>0.6 nmol/L). We discuss where the Exeter MODY probability calculator can help and where it may misclassify non‑European patients, and propose practical triggers for ordering an NGS panel to avoid years of mislabeling.

blogs.title: De‑glucotoxicize, then de‑escalate: how a genetic answer changes the diabetes Rx
blogs.description: Using the case’s A1c 10.2% presentation, we review a pragmatic initial plan—short‑term basal insulin to reverse glucotoxicity—followed by targeted de‑escalation once HNF1A‑MODY is confirmed. We compare low‑dose sulfonylureas (classic first‑line) with GLP‑1 receptor agonists as beta‑cell function wanes, noting trial data showing similar glycemic effects but less hypoglycemia with GLP‑1 RAs. We outline how and when to step down to metformin plus a DPP‑4 inhibitor for maintenance, monitoring for hypoglycemia and GI adverse effects, and counseling patients about the expected trajectory.

blogs.title: When SGLT2 is already turned down: why HNF1A‑MODY and SGLT2 inhibitors don’t mix
blogs.description: HNF1A drives SGLT2 expression; loss‑of‑function variants lower the renal glucose threshold and cause baseline glycosuria. We explain why adding an SGLT2 inhibitor in HNF1A‑MODY can amplify osmotic diuresis, dehydration, and hypotension, and may precipitate euglycemic DKA—risks that can outweigh benefits in this genotype. The post offers practical guidance on avoiding SGLT2 inhibitors here, safer alternatives for cardio‑metabolic benefit, and sick‑day rules if a patient is already on one.

blogs.title: Beyond ClinVar: calling a novel HNF1A variant pathogenic without overcalling it
blogs.description: We walk through real‑world ACMG variant interpretation using the case’s novel HNF1A p.N270S: domain‑level evidence (DNA‑binding, PM1), absence from population databases (PM2), segregation with disease (PP1), computational support such as AlphaMissense (PP3), and a highly specific phenotype (PP4). The post covers how to communicate P vs likely pathogenic vs VUS to patients, when it’s reasonable to act clinically while confirmation evolves, and how to leverage cascade testing to tighten classification and improve family outcomes.

blogs.title: MODY in an obesogenic world: why BMI and triglycerides won’t save you from a missed diagnosis
blogs.description: This case carried metabolic syndrome signals (TG 4.31 mmol/L, low HDL) despite HNF1A‑MODY, underscoring how rising obesity blurs phenotype boundaries. We discuss why BMI, acanthosis, or dyslipidemia can no longer safely exclude monogenic diabetes, and how polygenic modifiers and environment shape expression. We review adjunctive, imperfect clues such as low hs‑CRP in HNF1A‑MODY and emphasize inclusive testing thresholds, especially in under‑studied non‑European populations.

blogs.title: The sweat test surprise: small‑fiber autonomic neuropathy at MODY diagnosis
blogs.description: Severely reduced sudomotor function at presentation is a reminder that neuropathy tracks glycemic exposure more than diabetes label. We examine the role and limitations of electrochemical skin conductance (eg, Sudoscan) for early small‑fiber detection, how to interpret abnormal results at diagnosis, and what to do next: intensify glycemic control, optimize BP/lipids, foot care, and symptom‑directed therapy. We highlight research gaps on genotype‑specific neuropathy risk and when to repeat autonomic testing.
